q: How do I connect an ESP32 to Nodrix over the always-on WebSocket?
What is the difference between Nodrix.begin() and Nodrix.beginHTTP()?
a: `begin()` holds an always-on WebSocket — use it for mains-powered controllers that need zero-latency writes, and call `Nodrix.run()` every `loop()`. `beginHTTP()` uses request/response instead, for battery nodes that wake, report and sleep; call `Nodrix.poll()` once on each wake. There is no session to keep alive in HTTP mode.

How do I connect through more than one Wi-Fi network?
What value types can Nodrix.send() take?
How do I make sure queued data actually leaves the device?
a: Call `Nodrix.flush()`. Sends are buffered and normally drain on the next `run()` or `poll()`, which is fine for a continuously running sketch. Flush explicitly when you are about to deep-sleep or reset, otherwise the last readings can die in the buffer.

q: How do I send an event rather than a variable update?
a:
`Nodrix.event()` takes a name, and optionally a JSON payload for structured detail.

```cpp
Nodrix.event("door_opened");
```

Use events for things that happen at a moment in time; use `send()` for values that have a current reading.

q: How do I run code when the device connects or drops?
Is the TLS connection validated by default?
a: No. Nodrix runs unvalidated TLS by default, which encrypts traffic but does not prove you are talking to the right server. Pin the connection before `begin()` with `Nodrix.setCACert(pem)` or `Nodrix.setFingerprint(fp)`. `Nodrix.setInsecure()` restores the unvalidated default if you need it explicitly.

q: How do I pin a root certificate?
How do I turn on debug logging?
a: Call `Nodrix.setDebug(true)` before `begin()` and the library prints connection and transport detail to `Serial`. Open the serial monitor at the baud rate you passed to `Serial.begin()`.

q: Which port does Nodrix use, and can I change it?
a: Port 443. Every `begin()` and `beginHTTP()` overload takes an optional trailing `uint16_t port` that defaults to 443, so pass your own only when pointing at a self-hosted deployment on a different port.

q: How do I build a battery sensor that sleeps between readings?
Do I need to call Nodrix.run() in HTTP mode?
a: No. `run()` services the WebSocket and belongs in `loop()` for `begin()` sketches. In HTTP mode you call `poll()` instead, once per wake — it flushes what you queued and applies any control writes waiting for the device.

q: What do I need to include to use Nodrix?
a:
One header, and the library exposes a ready-made global object called `Nodrix` — you never construct one yourself.

```cpp
#include <Nodrix.h>
```

It depends on ArduinoJson and WebSocketsClient; install both from the Library Manager alongside Nodrix.

q: What happens to a command sent while my device is asleep?
a: It waits. Control writes are queued and delivered at-least-once — the cloud holds a write until the device acknowledges it and re-delivers anything outstanding when the device reconnects or next polls. Nothing is lost across a nap or a Wi-Fi blip.

q: Can I check whether a control variable has ever been set?
a: Yes — `value.isNull()` is true when the cloud has no value for that variable yet. Return early on null rather than acting on a default, otherwise a fresh device applies 0 or an empty string on its first connect.
